tip: Accusative masculine: after 'einen' the adjective ends in -en. So 'einen guten Tag', not 'einen gut Tag'.
'nach' shows direction toward cities and countries and drops the article: 'nach München'.
Modal plus passive: the main verb becomes past participle plus 'werden' at the end, as in 'konnte ... zugestellt werden'.
German has no -ing tense. 'gerade' marks something happening right now: 'lernt gerade die fünfte'.
Separable verb 'ankommen' splits: the prefix 'an' jumps to the end, as in 'kam heute an'.
'eigentlich' flags a plan that changed: the intent was there but reality differs, as in 'Eigentlich wollte ich'.
'man' is the generic subject 'one' or 'people in general' and uses the er/sie/es verb form: 'sollte man'.
'sich treffen' needs a reflexive pronoun; 'uns' here means 'each other', as in 'wir treffen uns'.
'innerhalb' takes genitive, but with bare plurals people use 'innerhalb von' plus dative: 'innerhalb von drei Werktagen'.
'schwerfallen' takes a dative person: 'mir fiel die Software schwer' means I found the software hard.
'gegenüber' means 'across from' and takes the dative: 'gegenüber dem Park'.
'länger' is the comparative of 'lang': add -er plus an umlaut, as many short adjectives do.
Time phrases like 'heute Abend' take no preposition; say it directly, not 'am heute Abend'.
The prefix 'zer-' is inseparable and adds a sense of breaking apart, so 'zerstörte' keeps the prefix attached.
Instruments drop the article after 'spielen': 'Klavier spielen' means play the piano, not 'das Klavier spielen'.
The suffix '-weise' builds sentence adverbs meaning 'as it happens': 'Unglücklicherweise' equals unfortunately.
'sich erinnern' pairs with 'an' plus accusative: 'an den Namen erinnern' means to remember the name.
Genitive of masculine and neuter nouns adds -s or -es: 'des Projekts' means of the project.
